key_insight: The paper shows that good agent execution does not guarantee clear product-decision evidence, so unresolved choices should be audited with decision-specific intervals and witness populations.
engineering_relevance: For ML systems and agent products, the work suggests preserving structured decision context and adding offline audit tooling to explain why a decision is unresolved before collecting more telemetry.
method: Mapped declared observation channels and product-value contrasts to compatible intervals and witness populations.
Ran frozen experiments on two pinned model snapshots, plus a follow-up with supplied preferences and a deterministic extractor.
Used controlled multinomial simulations to separate structural ambiguity from weak identification and limited calibration precision.
evidence_signal: Across 4,800 frozen requests, all 36 conservative primary intervals stayed unresolved; a 2,400-call follow-up resolved 3 of 9 comparisons per model, and a deterministic extractor resolved 7 of 9 without model calls.
watch_item: The audit’s conclusions depend on the quality of the declared observation channel and may still be limited when calibration data are sparse or the decision signal is structurally ambiguous.
paper_title: The Delegation Blind Spot: Auditing Product Decisions from Agent Choices
